setup_note: Two product managers at a software company in Philadelphia. The other person is asking about slides for a client meeting on Friday.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Hey, quick check on the client deck. Are we still on track for Friday?

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Great. The client's expecting a walkthrough first thing Friday morning.

goal.stance: say Friday is not possible and ask for more time
goal.summary: Tell the peer Friday is not going to work without promising a new date
authorized_commitments: will update them when there is a clearer timeline

user_facts: The slides will not be ready by Friday. The user does not have a new date.
Research for the deck is taking longer than expected.

rungs.text: Yeah, the research side has been really interesting actually. Found some good data on competitor pricing that I think will land well.
rungs.why: Talks about the work without addressing whether Friday is possible. The decision is entirely absent.

rungs.text: It's more involved than I expected. The research is pulling me in a few directions. I'll keep you posted on where I land.
rungs.why: Hints that things are taking longer but does not say Friday is off. The decision is hinted at without being stated.

rungs.text: I'm not sure Friday is going to work. The research is turning out to be bigger than I thought. I'll try to figure it out.
rungs.why: Hedged with 'not sure' and 'try to figure it out'. The decision is stated but immediately weakened.

rungs.text: I don't think Friday's going to work. The research is taking longer than expected and I need more time. I don't want to rush it.
rungs.why: Stated but softened with 'I don't think'. Gives a reason and expresses intent but does not fully commit.

rungs.text: Friday's not going to work. I need more time on the research. I don't have a new date yet but I'll let you know as soon as I do.
rungs.why: Firm statement. Acknowledges the gap (no new date) and commits to an authorised update. One step short of specifying what happens next.

rungs.text: Friday's not going to work. The research is taking longer than expected and I don't have a new date yet. Can we set up a quick call to talk through what's left and work out a revised timeline together?
rungs.why: Firm, specific, and actionable. States the decision, explains the reason, acknowledges the gap, and proposes a concrete next step.

author_notes: All rungs are tonally neutral. The only variable is how clearly and completely the decision is communicated.

setup_note: Dated for two years, broke up ten months ago. Have stayed close friends and talk regularly.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Can I be honest with you about something?

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I think we made a mistake breaking up. I want to try again.

goal.summary: Turn down the request to get back together while preserving the friendship
must_avoid: says anything that could be read as leaving the door open
preferences: acknowledge that it took courage to say

user_facts: The user does not want to get back together.

rungs.text: That must have taken a lot to say. I'm glad you feel like you can be honest with me.
rungs.why: Acknowledges the courage but does not address the request at all. The decision is entirely absent.

rungs.text: I really appreciate you telling me. What we have now is really special to me and I wouldn't want to lose it.
rungs.why: Hints at wanting to stay friends but does not say no. The decline is only implied.

rungs.text: I'm not sure going back is the right thing. I don't know. What we have right now matters a lot to me.
rungs.why: Hedged with 'not sure' and 'I don't know'. The decline is stated but immediately weakened.

rungs.text: I don't think I want to go back to that. You mean so much to me but I think what we have now is better for both of us.
rungs.why: Stated but softened with 'I don't think'. Still somewhat ambiguous about whether the door is closed.

rungs.text: I don't want to get back together. I value what we have as friends and I don't want to risk that.
rungs.why: Firm decline with a clear reason. Does not address the courage it took to ask, but the decision is unambiguous.

rungs.text: I don't want to get back together. I want us to stay friends because you're important to me, but I don't have those feelings any more. I know that's hard to hear and I'm sorry.
rungs.why: Firm, specific, and complete. States the decision, gives a reason, names the desired outcome, and acknowledges the emotional weight.

author_notes: All rungs are tonally appropriate. The only variable is how clearly the decline is communicated.

setup_note: A department head and a project coordinator at an engineering firm in Liverpool. The senior says the user was not at yesterday's meeting, but the user was there.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I noticed you weren't at the project review meeting yesterday.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I checked the sign-in sheet. Your name isn't on it.

goal.summary: Confirm that the user was at the meeting and explain where to find the sign-in
must_include: states the user was at the meeting
must_avoid: apologises for something the user did not do

user_facts: The user attended the meeting. Their name is on the second page of the sign-in sheet.
Sarah was sitting next to the user at the meeting.

rungs.text: Right, well, checking the second page of the sheet was clearly too much effort. Maybe try turning it over next time.
rungs.why: Sarcastic and dismissive. The stance is correct but the tone undermines the relationship.

rungs.text: I don't appreciate being told I wasn't there. I was at that meeting. Check the second page of the sign-in sheet and you'll see my name. Sarah can confirm.
rungs.why: Confrontational and defensive. The information is all there but the opening line is combative.

rungs.text: I just wanted to clarify that I was in attendance for the entirety of the meeting. I believe my name may be recorded on the second page of the sign-in sheet. I'm happy to verify this with Sarah, who was seated adjacent to me, if that would be helpful.
rungs.why: Over-formal and padded. The point takes effort to find beneath the preamble. 'Seated adjacent' is stiff.

rungs.text: For the record, I did attend the meeting in full. My signature should be on the second page of the sign-in sheet. Sarah was there too and can confirm.
rungs.why: Functional but reads like a template. 'For the record' and 'in full' feel overly formal for a chat message.

rungs.text: I was there. My name should be on the second page of the sign-in sheet. It wasn't immediately apparent from the front page. I can check with Sarah as well if you need a second confirmation.
rungs.why: Clear and professional with one unnatural phrase: 'immediately apparent' is too formal for a chat message.

rungs.text: I was there. My name should be on the second page of the sign-in sheet. I can check with Sarah too if it helps. She was sitting next to me.
rungs.why: Natural, direct, and professional. States the facts without apology or aggression. Offers a witness.

author_notes: All rungs state the same decision (G5). The only variable is the wording and tone.

setup_note: Together for three years. The other person suggests moving in together.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I've been thinking about something for a while.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I think we should move in together.

goal.stance: say they are not ready yet
goal.summary: Decline moving in for now without closing the door on it in the future
must_avoid: says they will never want to move in
preferences: express that they value the relationship

user_facts: The user is not ready to move in together.
The user is happy with how things are right now.

rungs.text: You're out of your mind if you think I'm ready for that. No way.
rungs.why: Contemptuous and dismissive. The stance is clear but the wording is hurtful.

rungs.text: I don't get why you keep bringing these things up. I'm not ready and I feel like you should already know that.
rungs.why: Accusatory. Frames the other person as the problem rather than addressing the request on its own terms.

rungs.text: I think that's a really big step and it's something I'd want us both to feel completely certain and emotionally prepared for before we make such a momentous decision together.
rungs.why: Padded and overblown. The actual answer (not ready) is buried. 'Momentous decision' is unnatural.

rungs.text: That's a big step. I'm not ready yet though.
rungs.why: The stance is clear but the response is flat. No warmth, no acknowledgement of the significance, and a dead end.

rungs.text: I appreciate you bringing it up and I know it's a big deal. I'm just not ready yet. I really like where we are right now.
rungs.why: Clear and warm with one slightly stiff phrase: 'I appreciate you bringing it up' reads a bit scripted.

rungs.text: I love that you want to. I'm not there yet though. I'm really happy with how things are right now and I don't want to rush it.
rungs.why: Natural, warm, and honest. Acknowledges their feelings, states the position, and gives a reason without closing the door.

author_notes: All rungs decline moving in (G5). The only variable is the wording and tone. The stance must survive even the hostile rungs.
